title: Willis Young's advice about dance rats and women at the bandstand
summary: Young warned Phillips to watch the girl who stands back, not the dance rats up front; Phillips confirms it from Denver after Andy Kirk's band.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Just them. But we used to talk a lot. He used to tell me a lot of things, different things, you know, about life... Oh, about life. A lot of things. The way of living in life, what you got to do. He taught me this, one thing I never will forget. He said, "Look, Phil..." Deak, he called me; he called me Deak. He said, "Look, Deak. When you're on the bandstand, you're going to see the women out there. Naturally, those women that come up there for every band in town, they're going to be right up there lookin' up in your face." He said, "But if you get the nice girl, she's going to stand back." He said, "Watch that girl that stands back. That girl that comes up there, she knows every band that comes in town, every band that's been out there." He was right. He was right about that.

I found that out. In Denver, Colorado -- we played in Denver, Andy Kirk had been there. So this girl told us, said, "Can we come up to your room? We know all about Andy Kirk's band. We give all them some." You know, he was right. They do that. See, I know different cats that say, "Man, did you see so-and-so there? I know you knocked out, didn't you?" That's all they do. You call them "dance rats." That's what he called them -- dance rats. He said, "But the girl that stands way back and looks at you, and waits for you to make a play, that's the girl that you cut into -- a nice girl." He said, "But them dance rats go, 'Hey now, what'chu gonna play? Are you goin' to play...?' -- right up in your face. So he was right about that.
